corrosion_narrative: The average mild steel corrosion rate was 0.9482 MPY against the target of within 3.0 MPY, and the average copper corrosion rate was 0.0883 MPY against the target of within 0.5 MPY. Status: Excellent. Corrosion control was Excellent because both metals remained below their target limits during the August reporting period. Copper corrosion increased later in the month, so the movement should continue to be compared with ORP response and product residual control.
corrosion_chart_comment: Corrosion remained within target, with copper movement increasing later in the month.
scale_narrative: Status: Acceptable. Traced Product averaged 53.22 ppm against the 28.00-32.00 ppm Controller Setpoint control range, with 45.3% of readings within range. The last 7 days still showed about 87.1% deviation from setpoint, indicating the product issue was still present at the end of the month. Conductivity was also not maintained and averaged above its control range, so the Traced Product trend is related to conductivity; reduced blowdown, higher cycles, or concentration effects should be corrected before assigning the issue to feed control.
scale_chart_comment: Traced Product remained high and was still not maintained during the last 7 days.
microbial_narrative: FRC data was not available in the field data for this reporting period and will be checked during the upcoming service visit. ORP showed a visible spike response pattern during the month, and biocide relay activity was present, supporting an Acceptable microbial control status. Copper corrosion remained below target, indicating oxidizer response did not create a copper corrosion upset during the reporting period.
orp_chart_comment: ORP showed visible spike response while copper corrosion remained protected.
water_efficiency_narrative: Water efficiency was Critical. Conductivity averaged 668.76 uS/cm against the 570.00-630.00 uS/cm Controller Setpoint range, with only 5.4% of readings in range. Conductivity increased from about 633.9 uS/cm early in the month to 703.6 uS/cm later in the month, indicating high cycles, reduced blowdown, evaporation concentration, or concentrated makeup conditions need review.
conductivity_chart_comment: Conductivity increased and remained above the controller setpoint range.
product_efficiency_narrative: Product efficiency needs attention because Traced Product averaged 53.22 ppm against the 30.00 ppm setpoint and the 28.00-32.00 ppm control range. Polymer consumption rate averaged 41.6%, indicating product residuals should be verified with phosphate and silica residuals during the next service visit. Because conductivity was also high and not maintained, product control should be reviewed together with cycles, blowdown, makeup, and dilution behavior before changing feed settings.
proactive_support_narrative: No service notes were recorded for the August reporting period. Recommended follow-up should focus on the unresolved health-check items: correct high conductivity by reviewing blowdown settings, cycles, makeup conditions, and concentration effects; then verify Traced Product residual response after conductivity control improves. Check FRC and dip-slide CFU during the upcoming service visit to confirm microbial control, and verify phosphate and silica residuals against the polymer consumption trend.
closing_summary: Overall August performance for Candler main showed Excellent corrosion control and Acceptable microbial control, while conductivity and Traced Product control require follow-up. The primary action is to correct the high conductivity trend first because the Traced Product deviation is linked with conductivity behavior. After cycles and blowdown control are stabilized, product residual and polymer efficiency should be verified during the next service visit.
